chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jarir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meat that remains in the teeth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for what is in the front of the mouth, swallow it, and as for what is in the molars, discard it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on meat stuck in the teeth according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a nuanced ruling on *istinshaf* (cleansing the mouth) by distinguishing between food remnants in the front incisors, which are swallowed as part of the meal, and those in the back molars, which are discarded. This distinction highlights the practical application of ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily life, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and specific detail in fiqh. The ruling underscores the importance of intention and location in determining what constitutes impurity or waste during eating.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the meat which happens (to be stuck) in the teeth. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what is in the front of the mouth, so swallow it, and whatever was in the molars, so toss it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ishaq ibn Jarir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meat that remains between the teeth. He (the Imam) said, ’What is between the front teeth you can eat; but what is between the back teeth you must throw it away.’”
